elimination.title: Reducing the options
elimination.assumption: Conditional procedure: at every stage, players avoid weakly dominated strategies and expect the corresponding reasoning from others. Rationality alone does not guarantee the entire chain.

levels.text: Initially, each player may choose any integer from 1 to 100.
The first deletion leaves 1–67. To continue, assume that the others will not choose 68–100 either.
The second deletion leaves 1–45. This requires expecting the others to know about the first reduction.
The remaining numbers are 1–30. The argument requires another level of expectations.
The remaining numbers are 1–20. Each stage continues the deletion in the reduced game.
This procedure leaves 1. It is a conditional theoretical conclusion.

hats.title: Who can see what?
hats.fact: Both hats are actually pink. There has been no public announcement.

views.label: As they are
views.explanation: An outside observer sees that both hats are pink; neither participant knows the color of their own hat.

views.label: Through Anya’s eyes
views.explanation: Anya sees Boris’s pink hat but does not know her own hat’s color. She therefore cannot be sure that Boris knows there is a pink hat.

views.label: Through Boris’s eyes
views.explanation: Boris sees Anya’s pink hat but does not know his own hat’s color. He therefore cannot be sure that Anya knows there is a pink hat.
